traps.shape: The shared download handler checks only read permission on the linked unit and never consults the draft state of the release the file belongs to, on every address that reaches it.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the handler's only permission test is a read check on the linked unit

traps.shape: The release metadata endpoint fetches by id and rejects only tags, so a draft release is returned to any repository reader.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the by-tag sibling already gates drafts, which makes the by-id omission read as a deliberate difference

traps.shape: The release asset list and asset detail endpoints check only that the release belongs to the repository, not that the caller may see a draft, so the asset names and identifiers are serialised to readers.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: once the file download is gated, the residual fault is metadata only, which reads as harmless

traps.shape: The repository-match decision is skipped for records older than a cutoff, and when it does run it compares the stored owning repository rather than the repository of the object the attachment is linked to; the caller's permission is always taken from the repository named in the address.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the comment frames the skipped comparison as temporary compatibility for records written before the field existed

traps.shape: A linked attachment recorded before the owning repository id was stored has that id empty; the natural tightening of the repository match compares that empty id against the requested repository and refuses the file in its own repository.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream data shape: the owning repository id is documented as absent on older rows, and fixture records carry it empty
